claims.statement: NEGATIVE RESULT (round's cleanest): a publication digest binds WHICH publication a projection claims, not that the projection still faithfully renders it. A human hand-edit to human.md kept the correct digest and was NOT caught; only a forged digest was caught. Deterministic re-render-and-compare closed the hole at first-divergence char 2957.
On pristine source the verifier passes 9/9 checks, both before and after witness execution.
Per-fact source slicing localises a MAX_RETRIES 3->5 mutation to exactly 1 stale fact of 5; digest changes 571ac017d0a9 -> b8c42993004a.

Static compilation alone cannot produce an accurate human view of this fixture: whether the contract is enforced is invisible without execution. The load-bearing backend boundary is the WITNESS CHANNEL, not a service boundary.

The run's own canonicalisation initially dropped the structural 'kind' field, rendering every function as an exported constant with type/value undefined — confidently wrong and invisible to the digest because the digest covered the lossy form.
No formal frontend/backend service split is justified at fixture scale by any constraint observed in this run.
Whether two independent intake implementations derive the same DECLARED set is untested.
This design has not been compared against the existing Phase 0 Live/Experiment/Change toolkit; the reuse control was never replayed, so no claim is made that it beats existing automation.
